analysis:
The PR renames MiMo-specific idle calibration to ModelCalibration and extends it to ordinary EngineV2 and CBv2NativeBlockEngine engines. The previous gate required native MiMo (nativeTransactionID != nil); head ModelCalibration.swift:15 now covers all supported engines.

Security-relevant behavior I checked:
- Calibration requests still use synthetic token prompts and cacheEnabled:false (ModelCalibrationRequests.swift:52). They do not touch the SSD prefix cache or consumer plaintext, so T-041 and A-001 are unaffected.
- Calibration still starts only while the provider is idle (active.isEmpty, pendingSubmissionIDs.isEmpty, serviceBudget idle, nominal posture) and is cancelled on shutdown (Lifecycle.swift:161, NativeLifecycle:86). Cancellation, interruption, backoff and release waits are unchanged. Whether non-MiMo calibration delays an arriving consumer request depends on serviceBudget.idleCalibration, which is not in the diff (T-010, T-029 are adjacent).
- Observations are now buffered per request (pendingObservations) and applied atomically only after every pump and reservation has retired (ModelCalibrationRequests.swift:35-43). Late receipts are discarded when the cell is gone (Measurements.swift:20). startupWarmup receipts are excluded from rate learning (lines 42 and 128) but still counted as generation work.

Gaps for the next pass: recordRateObservation, applyRateObservation, EngineRateObservation, ModelCalibrationPolicy, calibrationPosturePermitsWork, modelCalibrationPrompt, EnginePrefillReceipt.measurementPurpose and calibrationCell are not in the supplied diff. Whether they enforce a pendingObservations bound, the calibration-versus-serving evidence separation, and thermal/low-power gating cannot be confirmed. The rate evidence feeds coordinator deadline and performance telemetry, which falls under the provider-adversarial assumptions in TB-002/ADV-001 and is self-reported anyway. I found no concrete regression in the supplied code.
